findings.reason: implemented literally as written, the guard either trusts no quiet stat-ing pass (the motivating second read still stats every directory) or the node has to guess the intended meaning, and an apparently inert §15 would be accepted by a live pass that happened to read inside the ~10 s window after a firing pass.
findings.text: §15 says "the tree's change generation is still the one that pass wrote" but also "Each report of a change starts a new generation", and only a report (a pass that saw a move, the slow pass, a kernel report) starts one; the detector pass §15 relies on for its cited cheap-second-read is the quiet pass that saw the crew write already reported by the kernel watch and so "wrote" no generation — leaving the trust condition undefined for exactly that pass

findings.reason: the reader is named and the accessor is a bounded implementation detail a node can settle locally, so the plan's mechanism is not misdirected, only underspecified.
findings.text: §15 requires `_reuse_covered` (a function in `reckon/metadata_index.py`, a leaf module) to "take the identity of every other recorded directory from that pass", but the pass's record lives on `_TreeSignal` inside `_FleetChangeWatch` in `reckon/change_streams.py` (`dir_stamps`, `reckon/change_streams.py:173`), and the plan names no accessor or hand-off path by which the read reaches it

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every symbol §15 names resolves on the current tree: `_fast_tree` (`reckon/change_streams.py:414`), `_reuse_covered` (`reckon/metadata_index.py:395`), `covered_dir_identity` (`:168`), `_dir_identity` (`:879`), `_invalidate_tree_views` (`reckon/serve.py:1443`), and the change handler's invalidation at `reckon/serve.py:2805`; §15 has no `href` to resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §15's five cases each carry a declared control (case (1) drops the record so the stat count returns to the recorded-directory count; case (2) keeps the old identity so the added file is missing; case (3) trusts an unarmed/arming-pass record so the case fails; case (4) trusts regardless of pass time so only the earlier moved directories are stats; case (5) gives the relayed invalidation a new generation so the read stats every directory), and the live acceptance names a threshold (`under 1 s` on the second pass) rather than an assertion that holds however the code behaves.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §15's logs and live-pass records sit under the run directory with a revision header and an `EXIT=` trailer, and its outcome evidence lands with §7's at `the-page-paints-from-an-index-landed.html`, not in a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §15's prose carries no version tag, ticket number or plan label, and the mechanism words it introduces (`generation`, `record`, `pass`) name behaviour rather than a plan item.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §15's trust condition requires the pass to have *written* a generation, while its own generation rule starts a generation only on a *report* of a change, so a quiet stat-ing pass — the very pass that makes the §15-cited case cheap — writes no generation and the condition has no referent; a node implementing the literal wording can make the record never trust the quiet pass, and the second read then pays the full sweep §15 exists to remove. The root cause and evidence check is sound: §15 attributes the second read to `_reuse_covered → covered_dir_identity → _dir_identity` stat-ing ~2,500 directories after a `_invalidate_tree_views`, and §7's close records the same 11.3 s second read "stat-ing every recorded directory after crew records invalidate its cache"; the reader-thread caller is named correctly and verified — `_FleetChangeWatch._run` consumes every armed tree's kernel report and calls `_invalidate_tree_views` whether or not a stream is open (`reckon/change_streams.py:516-534`), which is what an earlier review's first finding asked §15 to state.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §15 carries one deliverable (a read takes unmoved directories' identities from the detector's last stat-ing pass), and its acceptance is one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §15 declares `depends-on` `the-page-paints-from-an-index#s14` (plan.html:29), which is the section that shares `reckon/metadata_index.py` and the last writer of it among the landed sections; no relationship points at a wrong node and no needed dependency is missing.
